questions.stem: In a design review, a supervisor compares the evidence: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: empfehlen cannot be split because emp is inseparable
options.misconception: treats a full verb as splittable

options.text: verlegen cannot be split because ver is inseparable
options.misconception: confuses a prefix with separability

options.text: belegen cannot be split because be is inseparable
options.misconception: labels an inseparable prefix as separable

options.text: einlegen can be split into ein and legen

questions.explanation: Einlegen is separable, while ver-, be-, and emp- are inseparable prefixes that stay attached. The key is D, "einlegen can be split into ein and legen". Option A ("empfehlen cannot be split because emp is inseparable") is wrong: treats a full verb as splittable. Option B ("verlegen cannot be split because ver is inseparable") is wrong: confuses a prefix with separability. Option C ("belegen cannot be split because be is inseparable") is wrong: labels an inseparable prefix as separable.
questions.hint: Check whether the prefix is separable.

questions.topic: A pair of verbs that differ by one letter
questions.learningObjective: Distinguish a one-letter pair from a sound change

stimulus.body: In einer Grammatikübung wird die Form verlangt, die der Regel der Stunde entspricht.

questions.stem: On a site visit, a supervisor compares the evidence: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

options.text: fahren and fahren are identical, so there is no difference at all
options.misconception: repeats the same verb as a pair

options.text: They differ in two positions: a becomes ä and h becomes r
They differ only through a change of tense
options.misconception: confuses a tense change with a letter difference

options.text: They differ by more than two letters
options.misconception: overcounts the change

questions.explanation: fahren and färben differ at two positions: the vowel a becomes ä and the consonant h becomes r, so calling it a single-letter difference is wrong. Option A ("fahren and fahren are identical, so there is no difference at a…") is wrong: repeats the same verb as a pair; Option C ("They differ only through a change of tense") is wrong: confuses a tense change with a letter difference; Option D ("They differ by more than two letters") is wrong: overcounts the change.
questions.hint: Compare the stems letter by letter.

No, the sign borrows a dialect adjective

questions.explanation: The sign keeps the spoken umlaut form, so a spoken variant is retained. The key is C, "Yes, the sign keeps the spoken umlaut form". Option A ("Yes, the sign shortens the noun for the board") is wrong: confuses brevity with spoken retention. Option B ("No, the sign uses the standard written form") is wrong: selects "No, the sign uses the standard written form" where the rule in the passage requires a different condition. Option D ("No, the sign borrows a dialect adjective") is wrong: labels standard spelling as dialect.
questions.hint: Check whether the written form matches speech.

questions.hint: Noun plus noun keeps both capitals.

questions.stem: At a staff meeting, a supervisor compares the evidence: Welche Antwort entspricht der Regel der Stunde?

answer.exemplar: One cooking act, such as blanching, can be called 'blanchieren' in a general register and 'überbrühen' in a technical register, so two word sets name the same action while differing in register and tone.

questions.hint: Name the act and give both registers.
